ru.title: Универсальный синтез захватов через топологию контактов без привязки к объектам
ru.desc: CoToGrasp — это генеративная модель для синтеза разнообразных и устойчивых захватов роботической руки, обусловленных конкретными топологиями контактов. Модель обучается без привязки к конкретным объектам, используя канонизированное рабочее пространство, сфокусированное на геометрии захватного устройства, что позволяет достичь нулевой адаптации на ненаблюдаемых объектах. Авторы вводят признаковую репрезентацию, которая проецирует локальные характеристики объекта в единое пространство координат захватного устройства, отделяя функциональное намерение от произвольной геометрии объекта. Метод продемонстрировал состояние дел на датасете DexGraspNet и был валидирован на физическом роботе.

en.title: Generative Grasping: Smart Grips for Any Object!
en.desc: CoToGrasp is a new framework that creates various stable grasps for objects based on their contact points, without needing specific object data. Unlike traditional grasp planners that focus on stability, CoToGrasp emphasizes how to grasp objects for practical tasks. It uses a unique workspace that allows the model to learn from general features of objects, making it adaptable to new, unseen items. This approach not only improves grasping performance but also demonstrates successful application on real robots, showcasing its effectiveness in real-world scenarios.

zh.title: CoToGrasp：无物体依赖的抓取生成框架
zh.desc: CoToGrasp是一个生成框架，能够根据特定的接触拓扑合成多样且稳定的抓取方式，且不依赖于具体物体。这种方法解决了传统抓取规划中对物体稳定性的过度关注，而忽视了如何抓取以支持后续功能任务的问题。通过在一个与物体无关的工作空间中训练，CoToGrasp能够实现零样本泛化，适用于未见过的物体。我们的模型在DexGraspNet数据集上的评估显示，CoToGrasp的性能超越了现有的抓取规划方法。

papers.title: The Embedder's Dilemma: LLMs Are Better, but at What Cost?
papers.abstract: Abstract Large language models and dedicated embedding models achieve nearly identical aggregate performance across diverse tasks, but embedding models are far cheaper and faster, supporting a division of labor by task type.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Should you replace your text-embedding pipeline with a large language model? We answer this with a controlled, cost-aware comparison of ten LLMs across six families and 26 embedding models (118M to 14B parameters) on 37 tasks spanning classification, semantic textual similarity (STS), clustering, pair classification, and retrieval. In aggregate the two paradigms are effectively tied: the best LLM (Gemini 3.1 Pro, 77.6) and the best embedding model (77.2) differ by 0.4 points. Their strengths differ by task: LLMs lead on reasoning-heavy retrieval, embedding models lead on classification, and the two match on clustering, STS, and pair classification. Reaching that parity is expensive. An LLM costs up to 1,431x more than an embedding model of comparable quality (USD 154 vs. USD 0.11 per benchmark pass), and the open LLMs tested process tokens 2.5 to 736x more slowly on the same GPU. Reasoning tokens account for 28 to 81% of LLM inference cost; lower reasoning budgets preserve or improve retrieval quality for most models in our ablation. The Pareto frontier contains the leading embedding models and one LLM, Gemini 3.1 Pro. These results support a division of labour: use embedding models for similarity, classification, and clustering, and reserve LLMs for reasoning-intensive retrieval. Our code, datasets, and results are publicly available at https://github.com/embeddings-benchmark/embedders-dilemma.

ru.title: Выбирай инструмент по задаче: когда embedding модели эффективнее дорогих LLM
ru.desc: Исследование сравнивает производительность больших языковых моделей (LLM) и специализированных моделей вложений (embedding models) на 37 различных задачах обработки текста. Результаты показывают, что обе парадигмы достигают практически одинакового качества (разница всего 0.4 точки), но embedding модели значительно дешевле и быстрее - в 1431 раз экономнее по стоимости. LLM лучше справляются с рассуждениями при поиске релевантной информации, а embedding модели доминируют в задачах классификации. Авторы рекомендуют разделение труда: использовать компактные embedding модели для сходства текстов и кластеризации, а LLM применять только для сложных задач требующих глубокого рассуждения.

en.title: Optimize Your Model Choice: Use Embeddings for Efficiency, LLMs for Reasoning!
en.desc: This paper compares the performance and cost-effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) and embedding models across various tasks. It finds that while both types of models achieve similar overall performance, embedding models are significantly cheaper and faster to use. The study highlights that LLMs excel in reasoning-heavy tasks like retrieval, whereas embedding models perform better in classification tasks. The authors suggest a strategic use of both models, recommending embedding models for tasks like similarity and classification, while reserving LLMs for more complex reasoning tasks.

zh.title: 根据任务选择模型：嵌入模型与大型语言模型的最佳搭配
zh.desc: 这篇论文比较了大型语言模型（LLM）和专用嵌入模型在多种任务上的表现。研究发现，尽管两者在整体性能上相似，但嵌入模型在成本和速度上更具优势。具体来说，LLM在推理密集型检索任务中表现更好，而嵌入模型在分类任务中更为出色。作者建议根据任务类型选择模型：对于相似性、分类和聚类任务使用嵌入模型，而将LLM保留用于推理密集的检索任务。

papers.title: QuoteBench: How Matched Scores Can Hide Command-Path Failures
papers.abstract: Abstract QuoteBench reveals that execution-boundary parsing errors significantly reduce LLM coding agent success, and disclosing the boundary helps recover performance, showing that evaluation must account for deployment configuration rather than treating matched scores as intrinsic model properties.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small LLM coding agents issue Bash commands through interfaces that may serialize, wrap, and reparse model output. Matched execution scores alone cannot distinguish command-generation errors from failures introduced after generation. QuoteBench measures this boundary with exact final-state validation on 56 one-shot tasks from 14 incident-derived families, crossing the generation contract with the execution transport around one deliberately unescaped added parser. Escaping at the interpolation point reproduces each replayed reply's raw-path outcome, so any recovery under a disclosed boundary must come from the model changing its generation. Across eight same-window configurations, replaying the same reply through the added parser lowers success by 55.4 to 73.2 percentage points; disclosure recovers 30.4 to 60.7 points for six configurations, and zero or slightly negative for the other two. Raw generation is nearly saturated at the frontier; boundary adaptation is what still separates models. GPT-5.6-sol's matched gap of -3.6 points hides -64.3 points of damage and +60.7 points of compensation. The deployment configuration reorders models: one reversal among 26 comparable pairs is unambiguous and four more sit on single-task margins. Evaluations of command-issuing agents should report the model configuration, generation contract, execution path, operating point, and final-state validator rather than treat a matched score as an intrinsic model property.

ru.title: Граница выполнения важнее, чем глубина обучения: как конфигурация развёртывания переоценивает возможности LLM агентов
ru.desc: В статье QuoteBench исследуется проблема парсирования Bash команд в LLM кодировании агентах, которые взаимодействуют через различные интерфейсы сериализации и переинтерпретации. Авторы показывают, что ошибки на границе между генерацией команд и их выполнением значительно снижают успешность работы моделей, скрывая истинное качество. Через точную валидацию финального состояния на 56 задачах они демонстрируют, что раскрытие информации о границе выполнения позволяет моделям компенсировать ошибки парсирования и восстановить производительность на 30-60 процентных пункта. Исследование подтверждает, что оценка агентов должна учитывать конфигурацию развёртывания, а не рассматривать совпадающие баллы как внутреннее свойство модели.

en.title: Understanding Execution Boundaries for Better LLM Performance
en.desc: This paper discusses how errors in parsing execution boundaries can significantly hinder the success of large language model (LLM) coding agents when generating commands. It emphasizes that simply looking at matched scores is not enough to evaluate a model's performance, as these scores can mask deeper issues caused by the deployment configuration. The study introduces QuoteBench, a tool that measures the impact of these boundaries on performance across various tasks, revealing that disclosing the execution boundary can help recover lost performance. Ultimately, the authors argue for a more nuanced evaluation approach that considers the entire context of model deployment and execution.

zh.title: 揭示执行边界，提升模型性能
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了执行边界解析错误对大型语言模型（LLM）编码代理成功率的影响。研究表明，揭示执行边界可以帮助恢复模型的性能，因此评估时必须考虑部署配置，而不是将匹配得分视为模型的内在属性。通过对56个单次任务的最终状态验证，QuoteBench测量了这一边界，并发现生成的命令与执行路径之间的关系至关重要。论文强调，评估命令发出代理时应报告模型配置、生成合同、执行路径等信息，而不是仅仅依赖匹配得分。

papers.title: Listening Forward: Next Patch Embedding Prediction Enables Scalable Audio Learners
papers.abstract: Abstract NAPE uses causal Transformers to predict successive spectrogram patch embeddings for self-supervised audio learning without auxiliary components.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Self-supervised learning (SSL) has driven substantial progress in audio representation learning, though existing methods have increasingly relied on elaborate pre-training recipes to reach competitive performance. A markedly different pre-training philosophy underpins the most influential progress in language modeling and, more recently, in visual representation learning: rather than train encoders as static feature extractors, models are trained to predict the next element, a discrete token or a continuous embedding, from the preceding context. Autoregressive prediction thereby provides a unified pre-training interface that transfers across modalities, compelling the model to learn the underlying data distribution. We ask whether such a simple causal paradigm can yield strong audio learners, given that audio's temporal structure makes autoregressive prediction of patch embeddings a natural fit. We introduce NAPE (Next-Audio-Patch-Embedding prediction), a self-supervised framework in which a causal Transformer predicts each next patch embedding of a log-mel spectrogram from the previous ones, using causal masking and stop-gradient as its sole training signal. The design is intentionally minimalist, avoiding reconstruction decoders, acoustic tokenizers, student-teacher setups, and auxiliary regularization losses. Across six audio and speech benchmarks, NAPE achieves state-of-the-art fine-tuning performance on several tasks, scales consistently across encoder sizes, and yields strong linear-probing results. NAPE also produces structured attention patterns without explicit supervision.

ru.title: Предсказание следующего аудиопатча — путь к самообучению без вспомогательных компонентов
ru.desc: NAPE — это метод самообучения для аудио, который использует каузальный Transformer для предсказания эмбеддингов последовательных патчей спектрограммы. В отличие от сложных существующих подходов, метод применяет минималистичный дизайн без декодеров, токенизаторов и вспомогательных компонентов, полагаясь только на авторегрессивное предсказание следующего элемента. Модель обучается предсказывать логарифмическую мел-спектрограмму патча за патчем, используя причинную маскировку и stop-gradient как единственный сигнал для обучения. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что NAPE достигает передовых показателей на нескольких задачах распознавания речи и аудиоклассификации, хорошо масштабируется и производит структурированные паттерны внимания без явного контроля.

en.title: Simplifying Audio Learning with Causal Transformers
en.desc: NAPE (Next-Audio-Patch-Embedding prediction) is a self-supervised learning framework that utilizes causal Transformers to predict the next patch embeddings of audio spectrograms. This approach simplifies the training process by avoiding complex components like reconstruction decoders and auxiliary losses, focusing solely on autoregressive prediction. By leveraging the temporal structure of audio data, NAPE effectively learns the underlying data distribution, achieving state-of-the-art performance across various audio and speech benchmarks. The model demonstrates strong scalability and produces meaningful attention patterns without requiring explicit supervision.

zh.title: 简化音频学习的因果预测
zh.desc: NAPE（下一音频补丁嵌入预测）是一种自监督学习框架，利用因果变换器预测音频的补丁嵌入。该方法通过简单的因果预测机制，避免了复杂的预训练过程，专注于从前一个补丁嵌入中预测下一个补丁嵌入。NAPE在六个音频和语音基准测试中表现出色，达到了最先进的微调性能，并且在不同的编码器规模上表现一致。该模型还能够在没有显式监督的情况下生成结构化的注意力模式。

papers.title: FlowEvo: Self-Evolving Agents through the Co-Evolution of Workflows and Executable Skills
papers.abstract: Abstract FlowEvo enables large language model agents to co-evolve reusable skills and workflows during inference, improving accuracy and efficiency across diverse benchmarks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large language model agents can adapt to complex tasks by constructing workflows at inference time, but procedures discovered in one episode are usually discarded after execution. Existing skill libraries provide reusable executable routines, but are typically assembled offline and do not grow from the agent's own workflows. We introduce FlowEvo, a training-free framework in which workflows and skills co-evolve at inference time. FlowEvo compiles successful workflows into callable skills, stores them in a persistent bank, and uses retrieved skills either through direct execution or as context for constructing new workflows. It also tracks each skill's downstream utility and suppresses skills that cause negative transfer. Using a shared GPT-4o-mini backbone, FlowEvo achieves the highest accuracy among 8 baselines on the full standard splits of ALFWorld, HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, and MATH-500. On ALFWorld, it reaches 85.6%, 26.4 points above the strongest baseline, while using roughly one third as many tokens. Across 10 base models spanning 7B to 671B parameters, FlowEvo outperforms ExpeL in 49 of 50 model-dataset comparisons. Code is available at https://github.com/DEFENSE-SEU/FlowEvo.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Самообучающаяся эволюция навыков LLM-агентов в реальном времени
ru.desc: FlowEvo — это фреймворк без обучения, позволяющий агентам на основе больших языковых моделей одновременно развивать переиспользуемые навыки и рабочие процессы во время инференса. Система компилирует успешные workflow в вызываемые функции, сохраняет их в постоянную базу и применяет их либо напрямую, либо как контекст для построения новых workflow. Фреймворк отслеживает полезность каждого навыка и подавляет те, которые вызывают отрицательный трансфер. FlowEvo показывает лучшие результаты на стандартных бенчмарках ALFWorld, HumanEval, MBPP и математических задачах, при этом используя примерно треть токенов по сравнению с другими подходами.

en.title: Empowering Language Models to Evolve Skills on the Fly
en.desc: FlowEvo is a novel framework that allows large language model agents to develop and refine their skills and workflows in real-time during inference. Unlike traditional methods that rely on pre-assembled skill libraries, FlowEvo enables agents to compile successful workflows into reusable skills dynamically. This approach not only enhances the accuracy and efficiency of the agents but also allows them to adapt to complex tasks by leveraging previously learned skills. By tracking the effectiveness of each skill, FlowEvo minimizes negative transfer and optimizes performance across various benchmarks.

zh.title: FlowEvo：推理时技能与工作流程的共同进化
zh.desc: FlowEvo 是一个训练无关的框架，允许大型语言模型在推理过程中共同进化可重用的技能和工作流程。它通过将成功的工作流程编译成可调用的技能，并将其存储在持久性库中，从而提高了模型的准确性和效率。FlowEvo 还跟踪每个技能的下游效用，并抑制那些导致负迁移的技能。通过共享的 GPT-4o-mini 主干，FlowEvo 在多个基准测试中表现优异，显著超越了其他基线模型。
